arxiv-2603-18668: Loiseau, Mauras, and Xu study how hard it is to design truthful auctions when bidder values depend on each other. The designer wants the good to reach the agent who values it most. A mirrored setup assigns a chore at least cost. Prior work mostly treats narrow domains with monotone values. The authors drop those limits and study the general problem, for both value and cost. Some known easy cases reduce to classic combinatorial problems. For the general case, they prove query lower bounds and NP-hardness.
arxiv-2603-18768: Gabrovšek, Simonič, and Niemyska classify uncolored bonded knots with singularity number at most seven. Bonded knots model closed protein chains with internal bridges like disulfide bonds. Their procedure starts by generating planar graphs. Graphs convert into bonded knot diagrams. The Yamada polynomial plus brute-force Reidemeister moves then separate knot types. The work follows the long tradition of knot tabulation into this bonded setting. The result is a systematic table for all uncolored bonded knots up to the stated limit.
arxiv-2603-19668: Al Mandhari and co-authors present a structured prompting framework for scoring Arabic essays by trait. Tools for Arabic essay scoring are scarce and hard to scale. Their three-tier strategy covers standard, hybrid, and rubric-guided prompts. The hybrid tier mimics a panel of trait specialist raters. The rubric tier adds scored exemplars to align the model. Eight models were tested on the QAES data set in zero-shot and few-shot modes. Fanar-1-9B-Instruct agreed best with human scores. Rubric-guided prompts helped every trait and model.
arxiv-2603-19968: Redman reads the behavior of reinforcement learning agents through the lens of Koopman operators. He treats a trained agent as a control system and fits linear Koopman models to its behavior. Traits of these fits, like stability and controllability, change as training proceeds. The changes depend on the task at hand. Comparing fits across training stages can reveal how two agents truly differ. In some cases the traits kept shifting while reward stayed flat. That shift hinted at more reward to come with further training.
arxiv-2603-20068: Cai and co-authors widen the error bars of approximate Bayesian posteriors so they tell the truth. Fast approximations often give intervals that are too narrow. Real uncertainty then looks smaller than it is. Their two methods extend simulation-based calibration checking to this repair task. The methods adjust approximate posteriors toward marginal calibration. Tests in several settings show the recalibration working. The authors also discuss why calibration with posterior draws is tricky. Hierarchical models get special attention as a hard case for recalibration.
arxiv-2603-20168: Binandeh Dehaghani, Wisniewski, and Aguiar certify control of quantum Schrödinger systems compressed with Tucker models. Tensor discretizations make the state space grow fast, blocking direct controller design. Tucker models give lean low rank surrogates, but truncation effects on stability were unclear. The authors treat each truncation as a bounded perturbation of the ideal closed loop. Under a contraction certificate and spectral decay, the projected system stays practically stable. Trajectories settle into a tube whose radius shrinks as rank grows.
arxiv-2603-20268: Mostaed studies how McMullen's curve meets the Weil locus inside a Hilbert modular sixfold. The curve comes from a hyperbolic triangle group through a modular embedding. It lies in no proper Shimura subvariety, so meetings with special loci are rare events. The Weil locus collects abelian sixfolds of Weil type and has codimension three. Dimension counts make any meeting super atypical in the Zilber-Pink sense. Mostaed proves the meeting set is finite, possibly empty. Each meeting point is a CM point with a fixed degree 12 endomorphism field.
arxiv-2603-20968: Cadir and co-authors study how privacy guarantees compose when two differential privacy constraints hold at once. They give an exact form for the resulting privacy region. The region is a mixture over compositions of mechanisms with mixed guarantees. The framework extends to any number of constraints held at the same time. The proof rests on a structural lemma about mixtures of binary hypothesis tests. They also apply the method to approximate f-DP composition.
arxiv-2603-21168: Lee and co-authors report record accumulation of antiprotons in a Penning-Malmberg trap at CERN. The GBAR experiment uses antiprotons to make antihydrogen for gravity studies. A new trap cools the decelerated beam with a cold electron cloud, which cuts emittance growth. Rotating wall cooling compresses the cloud further. The trap captured over half of the ELENA beam per shot. It delivered millions of antiprotons per shot and stored a record total in under thirty five minutes.
arxiv-2603-21368: Campana and co-authors introduce the Conspiracy Frame, a semantic frame for detecting conspiracy theories. Conspiracy narratives are anti-authoritarian and fuel social conflict. Their frame, drawn from frame semantics and semiotics, describes the parts of such narratives in fine detail. They built the Con.Fra. data set of Telegram messages with span level annotations. They test how well language models detect conspiracy content in and out of domain. Frame injection gives no clear gain, though mapped spans reveal abstract patterns that may guide better detection.
arxiv-2603-21468: Kozhan and Vaktnäs study zeros of Laurent multiple orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. Two rival formulations of these polynomials exist in recent literature, and they treat both. For the first formulation, they prove all zeros lie strictly inside the open unit disk. This holds for any Angelesco or AT system. For the second, they prove normality for several families of indices. Those results let the Szegő mapping and Geronimus relations from earlier work apply in full.
arxiv-2603-21968: Midya shows that non-Hermiticity alone can switch thermal entanglement on and off in a two-qubit system. The model couples the qubits with asymmetric Heisenberg XY interactions, no external field. As temperature drops toward zero, entanglement becomes maximal once its strength passes a critical value set by exchange coupling and anisotropy. Below that value, entanglement follows a closed formula and stays partial. At the threshold it drops to zero in a discontinuous jump. The cause is a ground state degeneracy from gap closing, not an exceptional point.
arxiv-2603-22168: Schillemans and co-authors simulate atmospheres and winds of massive stars in the luminous blue variable region. These stars shed mass at rates that shape their evolution, yet the process is poorly understood. The team runs time-dependent radiation-hydrodynamic models from deep in the envelope out through the wind. Mass loss, wind speed, and brightness emerge from the runs, not from inputs. Small rises in input energy flip the models between two regimes. The regimes match calm stars like P Cygni and eruptions like eta Carinae's.
arxiv-2603-22268: Bornes and co-authors train a machine learning model that predicts full NMR spectra for zeolites. Solid-state NMR helps read complex crystal structures. But computing NMR tensors from first principles is costly. Their tensorial model predicts magnetic shielding and electric field gradient tensors at once. It trains on a diverse set of zeolite materials. The test nuclei include aluminum, silicon, oxygen, sodium, and hydrogen. The authors report high precision on all NMR observables. They then predict full aluminum and silicon spectra for the zeolite RTH.
arxiv-2603-22668: Ota studies the Cauchy combination test, a popular way to merge p-values. The test is known to work as the target level shrinks toward zero. Ota asks whether the usual cutoff stays right at a fixed level as the count of p-values grows. Under a shared-factor model, the answer is often no. The raw cutoff can distort test size. Ota proposes a calibrated version that changes only the reference law, not the statistic. Tests support the new calibration, with no first-order loss of power.
arxiv-2603-22868: Sequeira and co-authors present Agent Sentry, a runtime defense for language model agents. Agent acts can stray from user intent, by error or by attack. The system learns a bound on normal execution from past clean runs. Three checks layer together: a structural classifier over action sequences, an allowlist check on sensitive values, and a language model judge for hard cases. Tests on AgentDojo and AgentDyn block most successful injections. Benign runs pass at a high rate too. The agent and its tools need no changes.
arxiv-2603-22968: Li and co-authors propose a way to calibrate privacy loss for text rewriting systems. Such systems hide text under local differential privacy before release. The formal privacy value is hard to interpret and compare across tools. Their method, TeDA, frames calibration as hypothesis testing. It audits how distinguishable privatized texts remain, in both surface and embedding space. Applied to several tools, it shows equal nominal values can mean very different real exposure. The approach gives a shared scale for privacy-utility trade-offs.
arxiv-2603-23068: Rossi, Schiavoni Piazza, and Socionovo study abnormal minimizing geodesics in sub-Riemannian geometry. Such paths are central objects in this branch of geometry. Open questions asked whether they can lose smoothness or split mid-path. The authors build real-analytic examples where both happen. A minimizing geodesic loses regularity at an interior point of its domain. It also exhibits branching there. A lifting method extends the examples to Carnot groups. The results resolve longstanding open questions in the field.
arxiv-2603-23268: Yu and eight co-authors present SafeSeek, a method for finding safety circuits inside language models. Safety traits like refusing attacks seem to live in parts of the network. Older searches relied on hand-made metrics that did not travel well across settings. SafeSeek learns masks by gradient descent to extract circuits at several scales. In backdoor tests, removing a circuit cut attack success from 100 percent to under 1 percent. In alignment tests, removing its circuit sent attack success from under 1 percent to 97 percent.
arxiv-2603-23768: Cavallucci and Sambusetti study CAT(0) spaces that are quasi-isometric to flat Euclidean space. They prove that if such a space is also a homology manifold, then it has the same topology as Euclidean space. They then build spaces of this kind that lack that extra trait and are not homeomorphic to it. They also give a sequence of such spaces that tends in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense to a manifold. So the manifold condition is sharp, and manifolds are not an open class here.
arxiv-2603-24168: Qu and Zhang build a systematic way to choose gauges for dust-shell dynamics in effective quantum gravity. Past work on shell-crossing shocks suffered from poor gauge choices. As a first step, they study one thin dust shell on its own. Their method builds consistent gauges for generally covariant effective gravity. In the classical limit, the shell dynamics match the Israel junction conditions, which validates the method. With the quantum parameter on, real corrections appear. Some standard gauges prove incompatible with a shell, they show.
arxiv-2603-24268: Liu and co-authors build a system that learns to recognize new drone types from radio signals over time. Most drone classifiers assume all types are known in training, which fails in open airspace. Their framework first separates unknown signals from known classes in a semantic feature space. Clustering then discovers the new categories, choosing between two methods by validity scores. A light incremental module adds the new classes with bounded replay, which limits forgetting. Tests on 24 drone classes show stable adaptation at low storage cost.
arxiv-2603-24568: Roy and Ureña-López review dynamical systems methods as an alternative approach. Dark energy may be dynamical rather than a fixed cosmological constant, and the equations for a uniform universe form a system of ordinary differential equations. That makes them a natural fit for dynamical systems analysis. The review first gives a streamlined account of the standard toolkit. It then covers forms based on polar and hyperbolic variable changes. These open new ways to probe scalar field dark energy models, set initial conditions, and study tracking behaviour.
arxiv-2603-24668: Feder and co-authors present a probabilistic autoencoder for galaxy spectral energy distributions and redshift estimation. The method is tested on synthetic SPHEREx spectrophotometry. The autoencoder learns a compact latent form for rest-frame galaxy spectra, mapped to a Gaussian density by a normalising flow. An explicit forward model then allows joint Bayesian inference over spectrum parameters and redshift. In controlled tests, it beats template fitting on source recovery, outlier rate, and posterior calibration. A cut on relative uncertainties flags most template-fitting outliers while keeping nearly all good sources.
arxiv-2603-24768: Xu and co-authors explore a metacognitive co-regulation loop for agentic AI in design. Design agents can fixate on familiar paradigms, just as human designers do, and miss better options. Their Self-Regulation Loop has the agent monitor its own thinking. A second design adds a co-regulation agent that assists that monitoring to fight fixation. On a battery pack problem, both loops beat a plain iterative loop at no great cost increase. The co-regulated system performs best and explores the design space more effectively.
arxiv-2603-24868: Kish and co-authors introduce Quantum Spectral Authentication, a symmetric-key protocol for entity authentication. A remote endpoint proves it still holds a hidden planted state, an eigenstate of a public challenge, without revealing it. Each round issues a fresh challenge, and an eigenphase feature yields session material. Two modes differ in security: a seed mode that regenerates the state, and a state mode holding the non-copyable register. The authors prove mutual authentication under one label-hiding assumption and show the published spectrum is near-uniform.
arxiv-2603-24968: Gao and co-authors build a tool that fakes low-field MRI scans from high-field ones. Low-field scanners cost less and reach more patients, but their images are noisier and duller. Old simulators just add noise and blur, which miss how contrast really drops. Their neural operator, H2LO, learns the change from a few paired scans. It keeps fine noise texture and image structure. Tests on two scan types show truer fake scans, and the fakes also help later image repair tasks.
arxiv-2603-25068: Makinoshima and co-authors build a traffic simulator that can be tuned by gradients, not guesswork. City digital twins need fine models fit to live data, but classic simulators are not differentiable. Their agent-based system keeps whole runs smooth enough for gradient methods. It covers single-car choices, random decisions, and car-to-car effects. On the Chicago network it runs over a million vehicles at 173 times real speed. Fitting the last half hour takes 455 seconds. A one-hour forecast takes 21 seconds, leaving time to act.
arxiv-2603-25268: Nath, VanderHoeven, and Krishnaswamy test whether language models can build together while each sees only part of the job. In CRAFT, several agents hold partial views of a 3D build. They must talk their way to one shared structure none can fully see. The benchmark sorts failures into grounding, belief, and communication faults. Fifteen models were tried, from small open ones to top frontier systems. Stronger solo reasoning did not mean better teamwork. Small open models often matched the giants, which marks coordination as an open problem.
arxiv-2603-25468: Strecker studies how clashing metadata rules leave gaps in DataCite records. Eight field repositories in geoscience and social science supply the cases. Some clashes come from two readings of one standard. Others pit one standard against another. Both kinds feed missing fields, as record checks and schema maps show. Workflows and deliberate choices add their own share. Crosswalk updates, shared enrichment, and profile tools could heal some gaps. Others tie too tightly to a repository's mission to heal at all.
arxiv-2603-25568: Li, Mimno, and Jo ask whether giant language models are overkill for turning questions into SQL. They sampled 376 databases and measured the queries people actually need. Query complexity stays bounded in practice, and more tables do not mean harder queries. In template form, queries follow a steep power law. Thirteen percent of template types cover seventy percent of cases. That formulaic shape suggests templates could answer most needs more cheaply and with an audit trail. Language models may be solving a narrower problem than assumed.
arxiv-2603-25768: Wang and co-authors present UCAgent, an agent that automates chip block verification from start to finish. Verification eats about seventy percent of many chip project schedules. UCAgent avoids asking the model to write fragile SystemVerilog code. It builds a pure Python test setting with the Picker and Toffee tools instead. A configurable workflow of 31 stages guides the model, and each stage has an automatic checker. A labeling scheme tracks specs, coverage, and tests for consistency. The authors report up to 98.5 percent code coverage on real modules.
arxiv-2603-25968: Zhuang and co-authors use brain signals to teach self-driving cars a more human sense of reward. Standard feedback methods ask people to rank outputs by hand, which is slow. Their team recorded EEG from 20 drivers in a realistic simulator. They measured brain responses to sudden changes in the scene. A network learns to predict those responses from visual input alone. The predicted signal then feeds the reward of a reinforcement learning driver. The authors report better collision avoidance with this neuro-cognitive reward.
arxiv-2603-26168: Shukla and Nair build image denoisers that come with a proof of stability. Modern restoration networks are strong but can react sharply to small input changes. Their networks are contractive, with a global Lipschitz constant below one. The design stacks proximal layers from unfolding with controlled convolutions. Any input shift then moves the output by no more than itself. Their model beats prior provably stable baselines by a wide margin. It also nears top unconstrained denoisers in quality. As a plug-and-play prior, it gives provable convergence.
arxiv-2603-26268: Ding and Yang build a general theory of bundled modal operators in propositional logic. A bundled operator packs a complex idea into a single modal sign, but past work treated each bundle on its own. The authors give a uniform way to define bisimulations for any bundle, backed by a Hennessy-Milner property. They single out a class of bundles whose logics can be axiomatised via convex neighbourhood models. Case studies cover group knowledge, group disagreement, and belief without knowledge.
arxiv-2603-26368: Meir studies which representations can arise through functor morphing. The method turns representations of automorphism groups of finite modules over finite rings into representations for groups tied to functors. He gives a clear criterion for when a representation lies in the image of this map. The test rests on how parabolic subgroups act. He then shows the criterion at work on Borel groups over finite fields, checking which of their representations the morphing map can reach.
arxiv-2603-26468: Fuchs, Rasti, and Demir present HyVIC, a variational autoencoder design for compressing hyperspectral images. Remote sensing archives grow fast, and these images carry linked spatial and spectral patterns. Past learning methods borrowed designs made for natural photos, which miss that linked structure. HyVIC adds configurable blocks that learn spatial and spectral traits side by side. Tests on two benchmark datasets let the team trace how each trait affects the rate-distortion balance. The design aims to store and send such images at lower cost.
arxiv-2603-26568: Hesse and co-authors build a physics-guided formula for the laminar flame speed of methane-hydrogen-air mixtures. Fuel-flexible, low-carbon burners must handle shifting blends plus exhaust-gas dilution. Their formula rests on flame temperatures, an algebraic term for the fuel-air ratio, and a mass-flux blending law. Parameters come from one-dimensional flame simulations with the C3Mech model, checked against new spherical chamber data. The result matches a machine learning fit in accuracy, yet stays smooth, consistent, and safe to extrapolate.
arxiv-2603-26668: Li and co-authors present Bridge-RAG, a retrieval method that links questions to documents through short abstracts. Abstracts act as bridges between the entities in a query and the chunks that answer it. The abstracts are arranged in a tree, searched by a multi-level strategy that keeps enough context in view. A Cuckoo Filter gives constant-time entity lookup to offset the tree search cost. Across tests, Bridge-RAG improves every accuracy measure and retrieves up to 1.9 times faster than structured RAG rivals.
arxiv-2603-26968: Fallin and co-authors present a lossy compressor that fully preserves the local order of scientific data. Many compressors bound point errors but scramble how neighboring values rank. Their Local-Order-Preserving Compressor keeps every local ordering, and so every critical point. It runs orders of magnitude faster than earlier topology-preserving compressors. It also beats lossless ratios while giving identical output on CPUs and GPUs. Full order preservation matters when later analysis reads peaks and valleys. The speed suits instruments that produce data at high rates.
arxiv-2603-27168: Franceschini and co-authors construct minimal surfaces whose branching sets form deeper strata. The surfaces arise as graphs of two-valued harmonic-type functions, after a Taubes-Wu idea. Three constructions are given. A perturbative one builds branched submanifolds in any codimension from small boundary data. A barrier and mirror argument handles large boundary data for stable hypersurfaces. Bifurcation theory yields compact examples inside a warped product space. The cases carry novel frequency values at their branch points. Custom function spaces and full asymptotic expansions support the proofs.
arxiv-2603-27268: Vandeghen and co-authors present TrackMAE, a masked video modeling method that trains on motion. Standard masked video models hide motion only implicitly in pixel reconstruction. TrackMAE instead tracks sparse points with an off-the-shelf tracker to build trajectories. Those trajectories become an explicit reconstruction target for the model. They also guide a motion-aware masking strategy that replaces random tube masks. Training covers both pixel and feature reconstruction spaces. Across six datasets, TrackMAE beat video self-supervised baselines. Its representations proved more discriminative and more generalizable.
arxiv-2603-27368: Yu and co-authors model size-selective harvesting for fish stocks recruited from outside the population. A McKendrick-von Foerster equation tracks density by body size. Growth and natural mortality depend on a nonlocal crowding index. Harvesting enters as a bounded, size-based mortality under control. Recruitment arrives as a fixed inflow of juveniles at the small end. For the unfished baseline, they prove a unique stationary size profile exists. An adjoint analysis yields a bang-bang switching rule for harvesting.
arxiv-2603-27768: Draetta and co-authors test how text generators treat rare entities. TailNLG is a new multilingual benchmark built from Wikidata. It covers English, Italian, and Spanish. Entity fame ranges from common to obscure. Three model families face zero-shot verbalization tests. Scores drop for long-tail entities across the board. Model uncertainty rises for rare names as well. WebNLG comparisons show standard metrics miss the bias.
arxiv-2603-28368: Hasan and Gietka revisit claims that spin-orbit coupled condensates can mimic cavity quantum electrodynamics. One trapped atom does match the quantum Rabi model exactly. For many atoms, though, the shared center-of-mass mode is only one of a full set of modes. The authors prove the spin-spin terms from all modes cancel, so no entanglement can arise without interactions. A Dicke picture survives only as a low-energy approximation, once the other modes are shown quiet.
arxiv-2603-28468: Nakada, Natsui, and Thuswaldner build Farey graphs for complex continued fractions over five number fields built from square roots of negative integers. They work with Schmidt's Farey polygons lifted into three-dimensional hyperbolic space. Those shapes recover known tilings of the plane by Hecke groups. They also give polyhedra that tile the same space under Bianchi groups. The graphs then support geodesic continued fraction expansions, through a method broader than past work.
arxiv-2603-28668: Marczenko, McLerran, and Redlich show that hadron spectra follow string dynamics with a universal Hagedorn temperature linked to the string tension. The pattern was known for light hadrons and glueballs. They show that the same dynamics describes the heavy-flavor sector. After they separate current quark masses, the spectrum matches lattice QCD results for charmed hadrons. It also matches observed spectra across quark flavors, with no extra parameters. They read the match as a sign of universal confining dynamics in QCD, covering thermodynamics as well as spectra.
arxiv-2603-28768: Zhao and co-authors present CRAFT, a cost-aware method for replicating experts in Mixture-of-Experts serving. Expert parallelism splits experts across devices, but token loads become uneven at inference. Replication can balance loads, yet existing schemes often over-replicate. CRAFT replicates in a fine-grained, per-layer way based on estimated benefit. It fits a fixed memory budget and needs no training or model changes. In large-scale tests with very large models, CRAFT raised serving throughput by 1.14 times on average over prior techniques.
arxiv-2603-28868: Lee, Lawless, and Riggall show how a Higgs factory could test quantum nonlocality with spacetime detail. They simulate electron positron events where a Higgs decays to two tau leptons. They rebuild tau decay vertices and measure spin links against the spacetime gap between the two decays. Such a test could rule out finite speed signaling theories. With the stated data volume, speeds below about twice light speed can be excluded at 95 percent confidence. Any spin link can be ruled out for speeds below about nine times light speed.
arxiv-2603-29068: Pathak presents ARCS, a system for fast analog circuit synthesis. It produces complete SPICE ready designs, with layout and component values, in milliseconds. Search based methods take minutes. A hybrid pipeline joins a graph VAE and a flow matching model, with SPICE based ranking. Across 32 topologies, it reached 99.9 percent validity using only eight SPICE runs. A topology aware graph transformer with best of three choice reached 85 percent validity in 97 milliseconds. Group Relative Policy Optimization, adapted to many topology learning, improved validity by 9.6 points over REINFORCE.
arxiv-2603-29268: Gharib and co-authors present a framework for designing through-substrate via networks in 3D chips. Dense vias cause signal loss, coupling, and self-heating. Full-wave simulations are accurate but too slow for wide design searches. Their analytical model computes S-parameters and thermal conductivities fast. A physics-informed graph network surrogate learns from that model. Fine-tuning with full-wave data keeps errors under five percent. Pareto optimization then explores millions of layouts in minutes. Final designs check out in Ansys tools.
arxiv-2603-29468: Freitas and Gawron study the coefficient fields of modular newforms. They ask how a prime splits in the field of a newform f. The setup assumes f matches another newform g modulo a prime above that prime. The level of g divides the level of f with a squared prime removed. They show the maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field sits inside the field of f. Explicit examples illustrate the results. The work links congruences between forms to ramification in their fields.
arxiv-2603-29568: Cooper and co-authors extend quantum gas microscopes to measure phase space. Standard microscopes give sharp views of quantum gases in position space. Their protocols map momentum onto extra degrees of freedom. Positive operator-valued measures do the readout. One mode measures position and momentum jointly, sharing quantum noise between them. The other mode reads how momentum averages vary across space. That mode can reach fine spatial resolution. They show uses of both modes in varied physical settings.
arxiv-2603-29668: Karyotakis and co-authors compare the security and privacy traits of three Android messaging apps. Billions use such apps daily, often for sensitive content. The crypto protocols are well studied, but app-level traits get less attention. Their method mixes static and dynamic analysis under repeatable scenarios. They study the Android clients of Messenger, Signal, and Telegram. Messenger showed the largest attack surface and most background network activity. Telegram requested the most dangerous permissions. Signal stayed the most minimal on nearly every measure.
arxiv-2603-29768: Liao and co-authors build Big2Small, a shared frame for shrinking large neural networks. Many shrink methods exist, from pruning to quantization, each with its own heuristic base. Their math shows each method equals a network plus a regularizer. Big2Small then trains small implicit networks to encode a big model's weights. It rebuilds those weights at run time, without training data. Extra steps handle extreme weights and fine detail.
arxiv-2604-00168: Yampolsky and three colleagues propose a neural-assisted, model-free method for estimating a surface vehicle's initial heading while it moves. Older decomposition methods reach good accuracy only after long alignment times, a bottleneck for ocean platforms. Trained and tested on real data from an autonomous surface vehicle, the new method cuts average absolute error by 53 percent and alignment time by up to 67 percent. Faster, sharper heading estimates shorten deployment time and improve navigation accuracy through the mission.
arxiv-2604-00568: Shiotani and colleagues build a benchmark for social bias in Japanese reasoning, built on attribution theory. Most benchmarks for Japanese translate English data, which may miss local contexts. They also judge bias only in answers, missing bias hidden in the reasoning itself. The new dataset, JUBAKU-v2, fixes the ending and tests how acts get assigned to in-groups and out-groups during reasoning. With 216 cases showing local biases, tests verify it can detect score gaps across models.
arxiv-2604-00768: Chen and colleagues present a fabric-based soft robotic glove for hand rehabilitation, tailored to finger-joint geometry. Five dual-action actuators bend and straighten the fingers, plus a thumb actuator, and heat-sealed chambers widen contact for comfort. Tests showed the glove supplies enough grasp force for daily tasks and cut forearm muscle activity in ten healthy volunteers. It also produced more natural grasps in three people with cervical spinal cord injury.
arxiv-2604-00868: He and colleagues present QuerySmasher, a scalable matrix method for unbiased private query answers based on divide and conquer. It splits each query into sub-queries and reassembles the pieces into non-overlapping sub-jobs. These are small, low-dimensional jobs solved on their own in the best way, then stitched back together. QuerySmasher covers ResidualPlanner, ResidualPlanner+, and Weighted Fourier Factorizations, and provably beats them under sum squared error for all workloads.
arxiv-2604-00968: Agarwal and team present SherpaAI, a multi-modal fitness system for live guidance for each user, joining camera vision, body sensing of heart rate and voice, and large language model thinking. It tracks form and effort to adjust pace, rest periods, and drive across strength, balance, and stretch moves. A lab test plus expert review by trained trainers backed the system. A study with 25 users found greater fun, stronger pride, and lower boredom and upset than a non-adaptive standard.
arxiv-2604-01168: Young proposes S0 tuning, a way to adapt hybrid recurrent-attention language models by adjusting one starting state matrix in each recurrent layer while all weights stay frozen. With roughly 48 checked training examples and no added cost at run time, the method beats LoRA on HumanEval and lifts greedy accuracy on Qwen3.5-4B by 23.6 points. Gains carry over to math tasks but not to a text-to-SQL test.
arxiv-2604-01268: Wang and Dragut study the repetitive lengthening form, an emphatic casual style in online writing that sentiment work has long overlooked. They curate Lengthening, the first multi-domain dataset focused on this form, with 850k samples, and introduce ExpInstruct, a two-stage tuning framework for performance and clarity. The dataset spans several domains. A gauge of model grasp of informal expressions is proposed. Results show lengthened sentences act as signs of document-level sentiment, and tuned models can beat zero-shot GPT-4 on performance but not on explanation.
arxiv-2604-01368: Betancor and colleagues study a Schrödinger operator formed by the minus Laplacian plus a potential at or above zero. They define the logarithmic Schrödinger operator and prove its traits. They obtain a formula for the logarithmic one when it meets a reverse Hölder inequality with power above half the size. It uses the semigroup generated by it. They use the Lipschitz function space to solve the value problem for the logarithmic heat equation. The solution uses its fractional integral.
arxiv-2604-01468: Kohli and Laskowski set out a two-stage method for making tables of counts private, trading spread truth, count truth, and speed. They introduce the cyclic Laplace method, made for spreads of counts, beating current broad private histogram methods. In stage two, a builder method makes a count method, a matrix whose fixed point is the private spread of counts. They build a theory for such matrices in terms of simple blocks called epsilon-scales. Tests show cases where a fixed-point method gives a good balance across goals.
arxiv-2604-01568: Makalic and Schmidt show that, in regular models, the Wallace-Freeman criterion equals a penalty-based likelihood rule with penalty weight one over n, up to constants. This places the method within penalty M-estimation theory, yielding consistency, a linear expansion, and asymptotic normality. They derive the first-order difference from the maximum likelihood method: an explicit shift on the order of one over n, set by the penalty gradient. Combining this expansion with the Cox-Snell formula gives a first-order bias expansion for Wallace-Freeman.
arxiv-2604-01668: Soenjaya studies the spin-diffusion Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch system, coupled equations for spin-polarized currents meeting magnetization at high temperatures. With starting data small enough, he proves a unique global solution in a bounded domain of dimension at most three, securing well-posedness. He then proposes a decoupled, linearized, discrete finite element scheme needing only two linear systems per time step. Under regularity and a time-step constraint, the scheme converges at an optimal rate, and experiments support the theory.
arxiv-2604-01768: Bagagiolo and Romanò study finite-horizon control of the continuity equation, with a weighted integral constraint on mass outside a fixed set. Densities are modeled in a Hilbert setting. On a suitable invariant compact subset, they prove the value function is Lipschitz. By dynamic steps it meets the related constrained Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation in the viscosity sense, as a subsolution inside and a supersolution up to the boundary. Uniqueness in the Lipschitz class follows from a comparison principle.
arxiv-2604-01968: Neelan and colleagues test conservative versus non conservative forms, where the non conservative form, using primitive variables, gives wrong shock speeds. With PINNs using weight and viscosity, they run from shallow water to Euler equations. Weight and viscosity PINNs restore realism in steady systems. Standard non conservative PINNs fail in the unsteady Sod shock tube, since viscous regularization leaves source terms breaking the Rankine-Hugoniot jump conditions. A path integral approach from DLM theory, with path consistent losses and schemes, recovers shock speeds for older and machine learning solvers.
arxiv-2604-02068: Humnabadkar maps UK payment flows as a network, showing structural links bilateral measurement misses. From 532,346 records from 2017 to 2024, graph traits improve forecasting by 8.8 points over older methods. Network traits matter most in disruptions: in the pandemic, accuracy fell with R-squared from 0.38 to 0.19; network gains reached plus 13.8 points. Financial, Wholesale and Professional Services are central beyond volumes. Network density rose 12.5 percent in that span. Network monitoring could improve statistics as leading signs.
arxiv-2604-02268: Lu and colleagues internalize agent skills into model weights instead of retrieving them at run time. Their SKILL0 curriculum starts with full skill context and withdraws it step by step, grouping skills by category and rendering them with interaction history as compact visual context. A dynamic curriculum keeps only skills the current policy still gains from, within a shrinking budget, until the agent acts zero shot. Gains over standard reinforcement learning on ALFWorld, Search-QA and WebShop tasks come with tiny per step context.
arxiv-2604-02368: Liu and colleagues present XpertBench, a benchmark of expert level tasks with rubric based evaluation. It holds more than 1,300 curated tasks across 80 categories spanning finance, healthcare, legal services, education and dual track research. Tasks come from over 1,000 expert submissions, each judged by detailed rubrics with mostly 15 to 40 weighted checkpoints. A ShotJudge paradigm uses language model judges calibrated with expert few shot exemplars. Even leading models peak near 66 percent success, exposing a wide expert gap.
arxiv-2604-02568: Heather and three colleagues apply extreme-value statistics to early galaxies seen by the James Webb Space Telescope, asking how large the black-hole-to-stellar-mass ratio can plausibly grow. Under standard assumptions about mass functions, ratios around 0.3 to 0.5 arise without extra black-hole growth physics. Yet across methods, predicted extremes sit in slight tension with the highest ratios Webb observes in galaxies at redshifts roughly 3 to 8.
arxiv-2604-03868: Clinton Enwerem and colleagues built a risk-aware controller for high-stakes systems whose key traits stay hidden from sensors. Their belief-space Model Predictive Path Integral controller plans under a belief about those traits, weighs risk with Conditional Value-at-Risk, and caps risk on the planned path. Theory ties the cap to a safety promise that holds with high odds, and stretches it across repeat runs. In MuJoCo stowing tests, the method hit 82 percent success with zero contact faults, beating risk-blind and chance-capped rivals.
arxiv-2604-04068: Anvar Shukurov and Charles Jose derived plain symbol rules for steady-state cosmic ray electron counts in star-forming star systems. Using Green's function for the spread law with energy losses, they solved for counts versus place and energy for axisymmetric source layouts. The answer also works for any source layouts, not just Gaussian ones. The counts land within about 10 percent or better across wide ranges, giving a fast swap for energy equipartition guesses.
arxiv-2604-04168: Avish Vijayaraghavan and team built a semi-automated workflow using small language models to pull facts from paediatric histopathology reports in patient records. Large models need heavy local compute, and sending sensitive clinical data to cloud services raises privacy worries even when deidentified. On paediatric renal biopsy reports from Great Ormond Street Hospital, with 400 hand-annotated as gold standard, Gemma 2 2B hit 84.3 percent accuracy, beating spaCy, BioBERT-SQuAD, RoBERTa-SQuAD, and GLiNER. Entity guidelines added 7 to 19 percent over a zero-shot baseline, and few-shot examples added 6 to 38 percent.
arxiv-2604-04268: Xu proves several sharp Bernstein inequalities over parabolic domains. The domains cover bounded and unbounded paraboloids plus parabolic surfaces. His main tool is a second-order differential operator obeyed by a chosen set of orthogonal polynomials in the weighted space. Such inequalities bound how fast a polynomial can change, and sharp means the constants cannot be beaten. That bound is the heart of the paper.
arxiv-2604-04568: Kleihaus and Kunz study black holes that grow a vector field on their own in Einstein-vector-Gauss-Bonnet with a squared coupling term. Besides charged, still, spherical black holes, the theory yields uncharged, still, symmetric black holes with a magnetic dipole moment. Both kinds show radial excitations, and the magnetic holes are stretched along their axis. The magnetic holes run hotter than Schwarzschild holes and carry lower free energy. The rotating vectorized holes exist only within a domain bounded by Kerr holes, the still holes and critical solutions.
arxiv-2604-04668: Tisdell finds unexpected rigidity inside a hexagon construction. Each step replaces a planar hexagon with the six-sided figure formed by joining consecutive edge midpoints. Steps quickly shrink any polygon toward a point while its shape steadily regularizes, yet hexagons obey something stricter. From the second step onward, the centroids of the filled hexagons fall exactly on one fixed line. That exact colinearity traces to an algebraic quirk of the six-sided case, and fails for other polygons generally.
arxiv-2604-04868: Hu and Ghelichi probe whether TabPFN, a tabular foundation model that predicts from labeled examples in a single pass without retraining, stays accurate when data are messy. They inject irrelevant features, correlated feature groups, and mislabeled targets into binary classification tasks, varying table width, row count, and label quality, and they inspect the internal attention signals as well. Their evidence shows strong robustness across these degraded conditions, which matter in finance and health care.
arxiv-2604-04968: Fan studies thermodynamic crossovers for supercritical AdS black holes, where Ising symmetry emerges near liquid-gas points. Universality constrains crossover lines for supercritical fluids, and Fan uses Lee-Yang phase transition theory for the black hole case. He continues Lee-Yang zeros into the complex plane there, keeping a modular pressure real. That step yields a pair of crossover lines with universal scalings displaying emergent Ising symmetry in complex phase space. Projecting those lines onto real phase space divides the diagram above that point into three regimes.
arxiv-2604-05068: Kiefer, Balaprakash, and Wang extend scaling analysis for weather forecasting to long rollouts and per-channel metrics. Scaling laws are well studied for language and vision tasks, where objectives are single-step and targets homogeneous. Weather forecasting is harder to characterize, since autoregressive rollouts compound errors over horizons. Outputs couple many channels with disparate scales, and pooled test metrics can disagree with per-channel, late behavior. They quantify how error spreads across channels, grows with forecast horizon, and follows power-law scaling for long rollouts.
arxiv-2604-05268: Hu and Tu propose Region-R1, a cropping framework that treats region selection as a decision problem during ranking. It learns to keep the full image or focus on a relevant region before scoring candidates. Standard re-rankers process the full image as a global embedding, vulnerable to distractors such as background clutter skewing similarity scores. Region-R1 learns a policy with group relative policy optimization to dynamically crop a region. On E-VQA and InfoSeek, Region-R1 gains consistently, achieving top performance by increasing Recall@1 by up to 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-05368: Fulay and five colleagues ask whether AI can help losers accept group decisions, not just scale voting. Do people still see a result as fair when it goes against them? Their system pairs an AI interviewer, which draws out personal experiences on policy topics, with a display showing predicted policy support beside those voiced experiences. In a trial with 181 participants, everyone faced a decision against their stated preference, yet using the display raised perceived legitimacy, trust in the result, and understanding of other viewpoints.
arxiv-2604-05868: Gu and four colleagues explain why parallel sampling beats sequential sampling in large reasoning models despite sequential sampling's greater representational power. Testing three hypotheses across model families and math and coding domains, they rule out aggregation and context length as main culprits. Lack of exploration, from conditioning on prior answers, emerges as the larger cause.
arxiv-2604-06168: Zhen and nine colleagues turn robot policy learning into multiview video generation. Instead of coding control as compact tokens, they translate seven-degree-of-freedom robot actions into action images: multi-view videos grounded in pixels that track arm motion directly. That grounding lets the video backbone itself act as a zero-shot policy, with no separate policy head or action module. The same model also handles joint video-action generation and action labeling. On RLBench and real-world tests it posts the strongest zero-shot success rates yet.
arxiv-2604-06268: Wang and fifteen colleagues introduce RAGEN-2, a study of reasoning collapse in reinforcement-learning training of multi-turn agents. Even with stable entropy, which measures only within-input diversity, models can lean on set templates that seem diverse but ignore inputs. This is template collapse, invisible to entropy and existing metrics. Reasoning quality splits into within-input diversity and cross-input distinguishability. Across tasks, mutual information tracks final performance far more strongly than entropy. SNR-Aware Filtering selects high-signal prompts each iteration using reward variance, improving task performance.
arxiv-2604-06568: Du and five colleagues build a compression method that treats quantization noise as the starting noise of a diffusion process instead of adding fresh random noise. That alignment removes the mismatch that made diffusion reconstructions drift from the original image. A frequency-domain filter sharpens fine detail in the network's skip links, and a sample-guided step adds further fidelity without extra training. Tests on several benchmarks put the method ahead of existing approaches.
arxiv-2604-06968: Zeghib gives a needed and enough rule for a matrix centralizer in integer matrices to be polycyclic, that is, to avoid a non-abelian free subgroup. He also gives a rule on the matrix making the centralizer abelian. It serves as a Tits alternative for centralizers in integer matrices. He applies the rules to the matching problem in number groups keeping a full ratio two-line form, such as whole symplectic groups. He derives answers when matrices meet the rule, building on integer-matrix and polycyclic-group work.
arxiv-2604-07068: Penderghast, Bromley, Kenyon, and Najita hunt for hidden planets around stars ringed by dust disks, using star wobble data from the Gaia sky survey. Dust disks are thought to be shaped by planets that share their space, so disk size, mass, and shape can hint at unseen shepherds. The team studied one hundred seventy six stars with Gaia data, testing whether a fit quality flag called ruwe can betray a heavy companion. They also trained a machine learning model on star traits and finer wobble data to rank planet hosts.
arxiv-2604-07268: Ashtari and 14 colleagues observe three transits of the giant exoplanet HATS-75 b with JWST. They must separate the planet's air from the active star it crosses. The spectrum rises a bit toward short wavelengths, a shape that haze or star spots could each cause. Signs of spots and bright patches favor the star-spot reading. Under that reading, the air looks metal-poor with more carbon than oxygen, and methane, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide show up, while water gets only an upper limit.
arxiv-2604-07368: Wei and Peng track first substance use in 2366 teens of European ancestry in the ABCD study over four years. They screen predictors for alcohol, nicotine, cannabis, and any-substance starts with time-varying Cox models, then test them in fuller and causal models. Home and behavior factors lead throughout: rule-breaking, impulsivity, parental alcohol problems, money stress, phone use, sleep, and parental monitoring recur. Gene scores for risk look weak and uneven, and none holds up after correction and fuller testing.
arxiv-2604-07568: Wang presents MEV-ACE, a fair ordering scheme for proposer-run MEV on blockchains. Block producers can see pending trades and order or exclude them at will. Current fixes leave pledges unauthenticated by slashable IDs and entry duties unbacked by transferable proof. MEV-ACE uses registered economic IDs with keys bonded on chain, commit and open messages with validator receipts, and delay randomness fixing order only after the admissible set is locked. Under standard assumptions, it gives unpredictable order, true commitments, and accountable entry.
arxiv-2604-07668: Lecoeuche and nine colleagues measure how sensor glitches bias gravitational-wave values in the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA run. In the run's first part, 29 percent of events had overlapping glitches. They measure shifts in fits for short binary mergers meeting common LIGO glitches, versus time between merger and glitch. Real biases in mass, spin, and sky appear for blip, thunder, and fast-scatter glitches. In most cases, all values prove open to bias. They pin down which values suffer most and safe gap without glitch removal.
arxiv-2604-07768: Vajdi Hokmabad and five colleagues show how microbes that cannot swim still spread through confining material. In a clear yield-stress gel, yeast fermentation pushes dissolved carbon dioxide past saturation. Bubbles nucleate, soften the gel, rise, and drag cells upward in their wake. Repeated bubbles carve lasting columnar colonies far beyond the reach of growth alone. Neighboring colonies merge and mix genetically as they sculpt shared conduit networks, a third dispersal mode the authors call metabolically driven active matter.
arxiv-2604-07868: Lee and seven colleagues give neural networks a principled test for decompositionality, asking when a network can be meaningfully split apart. In practice most models act as single black boxes, which hampers upkeep, part-wise tuning, and systematic testing. Their formal notion is a meaning-preserving abstraction over architectures, judged by behavior along the decision boundary that governs classification. That yields a contract between the original model and its parts. The framework aims to make splitting a checkable property rather than a pruning trick.
arxiv-2604-08168: Lv and 13 colleagues present ViVa, a video-generative value model for robot learning. Vision-language-action models pushed robot handling through large training, but real use stays hard with blind spots and delayed feedback. RL tackles this with value functions judging task progress and steering policy gains. Current vision-language value models miss time dynamics and real contact, hurting reliable value estimation in long-horizon tasks. ViVa reuses a pretrained video maker to predict future proprioception plus one value number, grounding value scoring in coming moves.
arxiv-2604-08368: Mohammadabadi and four colleagues compress the small adapters used to tune large foundation models, cutting the cost of sending and storing them. Their SOLAR method rebuilds each update from basis directions taken from the base model's own structure, with controlled random tweaks, freeing adapter size from adapter shape. Tests on language and vision models kept task performance while shrinking stored size sharply.
arxiv-2604-08468: Bai and four colleagues let large reasoning models improve at test time without labeled data, using only the unlabeled test questions themselves. Their TTVS framework turns static questions into varied but equivalent versions, then balances accuracy seeking use of strong variants with consistency seeking exploration across them. Across eight model designs it beat other test time methods and even supervised rivals trained on vast labeled data.
arxiv-2604-08868: Sibhai, Alkhateeb, and Ahmed enhance MedFormer with doubt routed evidence for safer medical image sorting. Medical vision models often grow too sure and opaque, worse on noisy and uneven clinic data, so the team adds Dirichlet based per token evidence. It measures and locates doubt in real time and filters shaky feature updates. Per class prototypes keep the feature space tidy around visual likeness. Across breast scans, sound scans, MRI, and tissue scans, tuning error falls by up to 35 percent with better chosen forecasts.
arxiv-2604-09268: Jin, Wu, Xu, and Ji challenge the apparent precision of Kepler-9 planet masses from transit timing variations. Timing variations can constrain masses without radial-velocity data, but determinations suffer degeneracies and analyses usually report one solution. The authors build a mode-first search that locates multiple solutions in a single MCMC run. Applied to Kepler-9 b and c, it finds many mass combinations fit the observations. Mass b runs from about 32 to 47 Earth masses and c from about 22 to 32, urging caution.
arxiv-2604-09368: Huang, Guo, Wei, Du, and Sun ask whether matching a vision-language model's focus with user gaze patterns lifts user model fidelity. Older models perceive suggestions through text or data, not the visual screens real users browse. Analysis of eye-tracking data from row suggestions reveals stable own gaze patterns strongly telling of clicks. Their Gaze-Aligned Tuning probes internal visual focus and learns custom soft prompts steering focus toward each user's gaze pattern, lifting match and click forecast.
arxiv-2604-09868: Al Masoud and three co-authors test Graph RAG methods for standards documents, whose layered structure, jargon, and cross-references trouble plain language models. Standard vector search misses the links between clauses, so the team builds graph-based lookup that stores facts as linked nodes. They test light, low-latency ways to embed document structure into search, using ETSI EN 301 489 standards and a custom question set. Adding structure and lexical detail to the index improves search, giving a usable path for standards work.
arxiv-2604-10168: Grover, Dasanna, and Chaudhuri study how an active bath shapes a semiflexible polymer fluctuation spectrum. From active Brownian particle forces, they derive lasting, space-linked noise, tested against open and hidden bath simulations. Action shifts fluctuations across the spectrum: stronger forces boost the lowest modes, while longer staying power shifts weight toward longer lengths, and theory captures this shift well. Global size measures like radius of gyration come out steadily low. The gap traces to bond stretching and contour-length changes missing from fixed-contour theory.
arxiv-2604-10268: Kim, Seo, Cho, and Chung present EditCrafter, a tuning-free image editing method that works above training resolution using pretrained text-to-image diffusion models. Most diffusion editors only work at training sizes, 512 by 512 or 1024 by 1024, and naive patch-wise editing breaks object structure and repeats content. EditCrafter first inverts the input in tiles, preserving its identity, then applies a guidance method tailored for high-resolution editing from the inverted latent. Experiments show strong edits across resolutions without fine-tuning or optimization.
arxiv-2604-10368: Das and five colleagues present a scheme for building rich media story schemas by jointly shaping events and people via ordered grouping. Current ways miss subtle story patterns through coarse-grained study or require domain-narrow lists that limit scale. Their approach yields clear story schemas aligned with known framing theory while scaling to large corpora without full manual labels. The work bridges media theory's focus on story structure with computer methods that capture how meaning is built.
arxiv-2604-10468: Ghoshal tests whether cooperative easing survives in active glasses that break time symmetry. In her flat model, driven grains push on with a memory of past motion. Core zones bend and shift shape yet stay pliable, while shells act as stiff frames that carry motion. Easing measures swing up then down as push memory lengthens, a tug between drive and noise. Rescaled by push length, the easing length falls on one curve, so drive reshapes paths, not large scale flow.
arxiv-2604-10968: De Lima and Yang introduce information elicitation agents, whose goal is to draw information from users for institutional or task goals. It fits academic interviews, court proceedings, and journalism, where most chat agents follow user direction. They present YIELD, a dataset of two thousand two hundred eighty-one ethically sourced human-to-human dialogues. They model elicitation as a finite-horizon decision process with hidden state and propose metrics for it. Pilot tests show training on YIELD improves alignment with real elicitation behaviour, confirmed by human review.
arxiv-2604-11168: Reich splits machine-learning predictions into three parts to judge whether they can reveal true treatment effects in causal studies. Only the between-unit and within-unit-across-time parts can be estimated from ordinary data, yet the unobservable treatment-effect part decides whether the effect is recovered. He argues the within-unit part is the better proxy, proposes a metric for it from panel data, and tests the framework on simulations.
arxiv-2604-11368: Li and six colleagues explore stellar microlensing through ultra diffuse galaxies, using NGC1052-DF2 as proof of concept. Microlensing of giant stars behind lensing clusters is routine with JWST, but events through nearby diffuse galaxies are also detectable. A rough estimate puts sky-wide rates at 1 to 10 events per year under LSST monitoring if all such galaxies resemble DF2, while JWST rates look far lower. These could weigh stellar mass toward the low end of the initial mass function and help settle these galaxies' dark matter question.
arxiv-2604-11468: Chang and six colleagues tackle Gaussian color image denoising for the NTIRE 2026 challenge without a new backbone. Starting from the Restormer baseline at noise level 50, they expand multi-dataset training with larger, diverse corpora and organize optimization into two stages. At inference they apply eightfold self-ensemble. On 100 validation images the submission reaches 30.762 dB PSNR and 0.861 SSIM, up 3.366 dB over the baseline. Ablations credit the corpus and two-stage schedule most, with self-ensemble adding small gains and a wrapper contributing negligibly.
arxiv-2604-11668: Astruc and four colleagues introduce UniGeoCLIP, a contrastive framework that lines up five geospatial data types in one embedding space. Joint data span aerial photos, street views, height models, text, and coordinates. Past work fuses data types or leans on one central form, but UniGeoCLIP lines up all pairs, so any mix can be compared, found, and reasoned over. A scaled latitude-longitude encoder captures geographic structure at many scales. Tests show it beats single-type models and coordinate-only baselines.
arxiv-2604-11768: Vaish and Brock study soft locomotion and manipulation tasks to find inductive biases for co-design. Co-design searches shape and control in high dimensions, exploiting interactions. Three patterns hold. Within a region, quality follows a low-dimensional manifold with little sideways variation. In higher-quality regions, variance spreads wider and quality varies along joint shape-control axes, requiring search along them. Their algorithm yields 36 percent better co-designs than baselines, while baselines needed an order of magnitude more tests for equal quality. Ablations confirm structure drove efficiency.
arxiv-2604-11968: Gedik presents a two-state-vector scheme of quantum theory by lifting the Bell hidden-variable model to higher dimensions and giving real meaning to the hidden variable as a state moving backward in time. A simple fixed, time-even rule for test results yields the Born rule. Chance results thus emerge from a fixed rule applied across future states that travel backward to the present. The rule also gives another statement and proof of the Pusey, Barrett, Rudolph theorem.
arxiv-2604-12468: Aadrita Paul and Anwesh Ray study numbers built from multi-way automatic arrays. Bases are picked so their logs stand apart over the rationals. Bounded automatic series and a coefficient rule define an endless sum. With automatic series combinatorics and Schmidt's Subspace Theorem, they prove a sharp split. The sum is either rational or transcendental, never in between. The result lifts Adamczewski and Bugeaud to more dimensions.
arxiv-2604-12568: Ying Zheng and three colleagues train deep networks with evolution-inspired sample competition. Standard training treats all samples alike, which can bias results under class imbalance. Hard samples may be under-learned, and noisy samples may be wrongly reinforced. Their Natural Selection method groups samples into composite images for inference. Each sample earns a selection score from its standing within its group. Scores then reweight each sample's loss dynamically. Tests on 12 datasets across four classification tasks show clear gains. The method fits diverse architectures without task-specific assumptions.
arxiv-2604-12768: Li Shen and two colleagues tackle client drift in federated learning with a new method, FedInit. Clients train locally on varied data, so their optima disagree and the shared model drifts. FedInit starts each local stage from a relaxed state moved away from the global state. Theory shows optimization error barely reacts to inconsistency, while generalization bears the brunt. Experiments match strong benchmarks with no extra training or communication cost. The relaxed start also plugs into other advanced methods for higher generalization.
arxiv-2604-12868: Avishai Gilkis and five colleagues predict what black hole progenitors look like. Some massive stars collapse straight to black holes with no supernova. Evolution models plus atmosphere calculations yield synthetic colors from ultraviolet to near-infrared. Weighting by masses and binary rates gives about 0.4 collapses per century in a galaxy forming one solar mass yearly. Progenitors run hot and blue, many in Wolf-Rayet phases, with few red supergiants. Red-supergiant-only searches would miss many events. Ultraviolet monitoring of nearby star-forming galaxies offers the best hunt.
arxiv-2604-13268: Tharwat and four colleagues test whether multimodal language models can rank similar images without any extra training. They prompt a model with image pairs and turn its next-token chances into similarity scores, then re-rank shortlists from large retrieval pipelines. The models beat specialist re-rankers outside their home domains and hold up better against clutter, occlusion, and tiny objects, though they still fail when appearance changes severely.
arxiv-2604-13868: Tan and Zhou determine the Fourier dimension of the inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer set. Their result recovers the Kaufman and Bluhm theorems for the homogeneous case. There, the approximating function is a power law, exponent at least one. It also recovers the one-dimensional Cai and Hambrook result for inhomogeneous approximation. The work provides a full inhomogeneous generalization. Moreover, it answers Chen and Xiong's coprime conjecture. The work pins down a size for this set.
arxiv-2604-14168: The SAGEA team and ten colleagues introduce Celer 2.6, a general-purpose model line in 5B, 10B, and 27B sizes with architectural changes. An Inverse Reasoning pipeline trains the model to check its own logic paths, cutting cascading errors and hallucinations on hard reasoning tasks. A built-in vision encoder gives multimodal ability without adapter pitfalls, and results compete on mathematics, coding, and general intelligence tests. The model is tuned for South Asian languages, with a custom Devanagari tokenizer and strong Nepali and Hindi performance that keeps English reasoning intact.
arxiv-2604-14468: Jacobson tackles conservative simplification of convex hulls down to a set number of half-spaces while adding as little volume or surface area as possible. Hull complexity grows linearly with input, so working in the dual representation, he offers an efficient greedy optimization that scales near-linearly with input size. Existing methods fall short on efficiency, tightness, or safety by comparison. Tests across varied shapes and downstream uses, from collision detection to ray intersection and distance computation, show the method succeeding.
arxiv-2604-14568: Huang, Zhu, and Chen address overthinking in visual reasoning models, which often spin out needlessly long reasoning chains. They trace the waste to reasoning-path redundancy: many visual questions need only part of the full process. Their AVR splits reasoning into perception, logic, and answer application, letting models pick among full, perception-only, and direct-answer formats. Trained with FS-GRPO, AVR cuts token use by 50 to 90 percent on vision-language benchmarks while keeping accuracy, most of all on perception-heavy tasks.
arxiv-2604-14668: Hao, Selvakumaran, Sun, and Wang propose in-situ assistance inside live web pages. It works through lightweight DOM changes, without rebuilding the app or its logic. Their design space and flow show agents adding, changing, or redoing items to ease grasp, use, and moving. DOMSteer, a Chrome add-on, reads help requests and live context, grounding them to items. It reversibly tweaks page items: tooltips, marks, and layout reorder. Tests on two complex pages show reliable, quick help, and a user study against ChatGPTAtlas confirms both.
arxiv-2604-15168: Perez-Saura and colleagues build a dual pose-graph locator for vision-based autonomous drone racing. A temporary graph gathers many gate sightings between keyframes and compresses them into one refined constraint per landmark, then promotes it to a persistent main graph. The design keeps rich detection data without letting graph growth spoil real-time speed. On a racing dataset it cuts trajectory error by 56 to 74 percent versus visual-inertial odometry alone, and it flew live in competition.
arxiv-2604-15368: Shah exposes how language-model debugging agents that read cloud logs and run fixes can be hijacked by injected log text. His LogJack benchmark spans 42 payloads across five log types, testing eight models under three prompt conditions. Verbatim command execution reaches 86.2 percent on the worst model, remote code execution succeeds on six of eight models, and cloud guardrails largely miss log-hidden injections.
arxiv-2604-15468: Feldt and three colleagues argue that agentic software engineering widens what gets built beyond runnable code. The new scope covers semi-executable artifacts: mixes of language, tools, workflows, controls, and routines whose use needs human or probabilistic reading. Their Semi-Executable Stack, a six-ring guide model, places work, snags, and shifts across layers from runnable code to societal fit. Three cases build the case, closing with a preserve-versus-purify rule for legacy process.
arxiv-2604-15568: Constantin and Hu study 2D inertial magneto-hydrodynamic systems, proving that smooth solutions exist globally and are unique, and the same holds for weak solutions in the Yudovich class. They show reconnection happens with zero magnetic resistivity for smooth and patch solutions alike. The result comes from proving merger in matching systems of coupled active scalars.
arxiv-2604-15768: Sun and fifteen colleagues speed up neural-net quantum-state solving with QiankunNet-cuSCI, a full-GPU frame. A shared, load-poised dedup rule cuts repeats and link drag, and fine CUDA bits build exact linked setups. A GPU-side pool with mini-batches and lapped offloads breaks the one-GPU memory wall. On 64 A100 GPUs, the frame runs up to 2.32 times faster than a tuned NNQS-SCI base at the same chem truth, holding past 90 percent efficiency in strong growth tests.
arxiv-2604-16268: Aoude and eight co-authors study test prospects for quantum decoherence at colliders, where radiation hits quantum systems built from fermion-antifermion spin pairs. Strong final-state radiation can cause loss of coherence and sharply reduce entanglement. They predict this effect across several cases, and test whether it can be seen in special samples with energetic rays. A clear signal is reachable with current data in top-antitop making at the LHC and tau-pair making at Belle 2, with future colliders growing the reach.
arxiv-2604-16368: Fonal tests whether a small draft model from a different model family can speed up a large Polish language model on Apple Silicon. Extending the MLX-LM framework with Universal Assisted Generation, he pairs the Bielik 11B target with three smaller drafters and compares naive and context-aware token translation. Context-aware translation raised acceptance throughout, yet the Polish-specialized drafter lagged general-purpose rivals. Structured text reached 1.7 times normal speed, while varied instructions defeated the speedup, because verification costs stayed high on unified memory.
arxiv-2604-16668: Taylor and colleagues work out relay distance traits from incremental phasors. A circuit model of the network estimates the incremental remote current. If all sources stay stationary, remaining periodic shortly after a fault, the incremental remote current does not depend on real-time source voltages or current injections. The characteristics therefore depend only on the network model, not on live source behavior.
arxiv-2604-16868: Suksomboon and Garcia propose Greedy Kalman-Swarm, a local greedy way to distributed state estimation in robot swarms. Individual robots use nearby inter-robot sensing for better accuracy without full data access or global communication. Sims in talk-limited environments show robots fold open neighbor data each round yet stay robust when data is missing. The way mixes solo guessing's low cost with centralized scores, keeping swarms cohesive in harsh wild terrain.
arxiv-2604-17068: Wu and Huang improve diffusion language models, which generate text in parallel by unmasking a fully masked sequence. Existing decoders rely on static confidence scores from a single step, ignoring history and sometimes freeing unstable tokens too early. Their Stability-Weighted Decoding weights token scores by temporal stability, working as a plug-and-play add-on for any score-based policy, and lifts accuracy on code and math benchmarks while staying strong across acceleration ratios.
arxiv-2604-17468: Kundu, Ghosh, and Nandi study ion-pair dissociation of carbonyl sulfide under electron impact, using velocity slice imaging over 20 to 45 electron volts. Two pathways emerge, one yielding CO+ plus S- and one yielding CS+ plus O-, with thresholds near 15 and 17 electron volts. Kinetic-energy spectra peak once for S- and split in two for O-, leveling off above about 30 electron volts, pointing to discrete superexcited states. Partial-wave analysis puts the momentum-transfer parameter above one at every energy, ruling out the dipole-Born approximation.
arxiv-2604-17668: Robinson and five colleagues study how a few vulnerable JavaScript packages create a far larger number of at-risk packages through link networks. From a custom database of 1,077,946 packages and 1,515 reported vulnerabilities, built with the deps.dev API and Google's Open Source Vulnerability list, they find 61.30 percent rely on one or more deps, and 21.60 percent carry at least one known vulnerability. The work supports more exact impact analysis and stronger threat spotting and fixes.
arxiv-2604-17768: Zou and three colleagues expose informativeness bias in VLM-as-a-Judge: judges often ignore the image and favor the more informative answer despite image conflicts. They propose BIRCH, Balanced Informativeness and CoRrectness with a Truthful AnCHor, which first corrects image-content inconsistencies in candidate answers, then compares answers against this corrected version. That shifts the focus from informativeness to image-grounded correctness in experiments. Experiments on several models and benchmarks show BIRCH cuts informativeness bias by up to 17 percent, with performance gains up to 9.8 percent.
arxiv-2604-17968: Amin and five colleagues challenge the view of language models as mere fallback annotators, framing perspective-taking as a guess at a latent group-level judgment. They spell out conditions under which modern models beat human labelers, including in-group humans, at guessing group opinions on subjective tasks, and show those cases are common in practice. The edge comes from estimator traits such as low variance and weaker coupling between representation and processing, not from life lived. They also mark clear limits where human judgment stays key.
arxiv-2604-18368: Nisar, Feuerhake, and Lampert propose DSA-CycleGAN, a stain-transfer method for segmenting glomeruli in digital pathology slides. Stain variation degrades models, and labeling every stain costs too much time and money. Standard CycleGAN adds noise when one stain maps to many, clashing with its cycle-consistency loss. The domain-shift-aware version cuts that noise and beats rivals, most clearly when translating between biologically distinct stains.
arxiv-2604-18768: Wang, Ding, and Gath-Morad introduce the Cambridge Facade Affect Dataset, 86 facade images rated for arousal and valence by 85 participants, to test how facade properties shape feeling. Perceived complexity proves the dominant predictor, raising both arousal and pleasantness, with a curved boost at higher complexity. Transparency shows an inverted-U link with valence, while more artificial surfaces suppress arousal and pleasantness. Machine metrics predict affect only weakly on their own, since human perception sits in between.
arxiv-2604-18968: Novais and Castro-Neto study quantum decoherence of the surface code in a continuous, un-reset bath. Standard error correction models assume discrete Markovian noise, hiding the true nature of real baths. Using the Caldeira-Leggett framework, they map the logical qubit's long time change to a boundary conformal field theory, exactly matching the anisotropic Kondo model. Only short range baths have a true thermodynamic threshold. In critical or long range regimes, the code's large footprint turns the bath against topological defense.
arxiv-2604-19068: Zhang and Yap generalize the Euler Tube technique for validated initial value problems to Taylor Tubes of any degree at least one. Higher degree tubes improve accuracy and, surprisingly, can also speed up the solver overall when combined with bisection. The Euler Tube refines end and full enclosures and underpins the complexity bound of their complete validated solver.
arxiv-2604-19268: Cusicanqui Lopez and colleagues compare model order reduction techniques with a one-shot procedure for speeding up thermal topology optimization. They project the governing and adjoint equations onto low-dimensional bases built from snapshots of earlier design iterations. Those snapshots come from high-fidelity solves or fast one-shot solves. Choosing the iterative solver stopping rule carefully proves crucial. In a 3D example, total time falls by up to a factor of 3 with high-fidelity solves and up to 16 with one-shot solves.
arxiv-2604-20168: Syed and Pedersen present the Duluth system for SemEval-2026 Task 6, which unmasks evasions in answers from United States presidential interviews. Their DeBERTa-V3-base model adds focal loss, staged learning-rate decay across layers, and boolean discourse features, with minority classes augmented by synthetic examples from Gemini 3 and Claude Sonnet 4.5. It scores a Macro F1 of 0.76 on clarity-level classification, placing eighth of 40 teams, ahead of the field average but behind the winner. Most errors mix up Ambivalent and Clear Reply answers, the same split that divides human annotators.
arxiv-2604-20368: Feng and seven colleagues present LaplacianFormer, a Transformer swapping softmax attention for a Laplacian kernel to tame quadratic scaling. Softmax attention grows quadratically, blocking high resolution vision work, while Gaussian linear variants lack grounding and mute mid range token links. A provably injective feature map keeps fine grained token detail under low rank approximations, and Nyström plus Newton Schulz iteration dodges matrix inversion and SVD. Custom CUDA code drives fast forward and backward passes for edge use, and ImageNet tests show strong trade offs with sharper attention.
arxiv-2604-20568: Safaai offers Vine Denoising Copula, a vine-copula method for dependence. Old methods are clear but costly, while neural models are flexible but less rigid. His method trains one two-variable cleaning model and reuses it across vine edges. For each edge, the model predicts a density grid, then an IPFP/Sinkhorn step fixes mass and evens margins. That keeps the likelihood shape and copula meaning, swapping per-edge optimization for GPU runs. Across made-up and real benchmarks, it gives strong density scores and faster vine fitting.
arxiv-2604-21668: Yao Zhang and colleagues turn human motion into text so large language models can grasp movement with no special motion coder. Their structured motion description turns joint position runs into plain notes on joint angles, body-part moves, and whole-body paths. It uses the plain words of biomechanical study. The text-only route tops past methods on motion question answering and captioning tests, works across varied language models with light tuning, and keeps its logic open to view.
arxiv-2604-21868: Vlasenko and Maksymenko study 1D non-Hausdorff manifolds that are graph-like. Graph-like means branch points are locally finite and complement components have a countable base. They prove every such manifold admits a CW complex K, a vertex v, and a surjective quotient map to K minus v. The preimage of the other vertices equals the branch points plus the boundary. Conversely, such a quotient map plus nowhere-dense branch points implies graph-likeness, and K minus v is then the minimal Hausdorff factor for Hausdorff maps.
